  "text": "The first envelope contained a photograph of my kitchen, taken from inside the refrigerator.

I assumed it was a joke.

My brother had helped me move in. He knew where I kept the milk, how easily I frightened.

I called him.

“Look at the date,” he said.

Tomorrow.

In the photograph, a glass lay broken beside my bare foot.

I wore shoes all day. Nothing happened until evening, when I dropped a tumbler while washing up.

The next envelope arrived beneath my bedroom door.

This photograph showed me asleep, one arm hanging over the mattress. Something pale held my hand.

I stripped the bed. Checked underneath. Slept on the sofa.

In the morning, my palm smelled of lavender soap.

My grandmother’s soap.

She had been buried with a bar because, towards the end, she feared arriving somewhere without being able to wash.

The third photograph showed my front door standing open.

Beyond it was her old hallway.

I could see the stairlift, the umbrella stand, the little patch of wallpaper I had peeled away as a child.

On the back, in her handwriting:

You left something here.

I burned the photograph over the sink.

That night, someone knocked.

“Keep it,” I said through the door.

A long silence followed.

Then an envelope slid across the floor.

Inside was a photograph of my grandmother’s kitchen table. My baby teeth were arranged around a saucer, each labelled with a date.

There was one empty space.

I touched the loose tooth at the back of my mouth.

Outside, she rattled a little tin.

“I’ve still got your pound,” she said."
